newsitem.title: JAPAN: Leaking Japan supertanker steaming towards berth.
newsitem.headline: Leaking Japan supertanker steaming towards berth.

text.p: A supertanker that leaked crude oil after hitting a reef in Tokyo Bay was moving towards a refinery berth at Kawasaki, south of Tokyo, under its own power, a coastguard spokesman said on Wednesday.
The Panamanian-registered supertanker Diamond Grace was expected to take about an hour to reach the Kawasaki Sea Berth, a spokesman for the regional coastguard headquarters in Yokohama said.

The 259,999-deadweight tonne tanker struck the undersea Nakanose reef off Yokohama, one of the most well-known undersea hazards in Tokyo Bay, on Wednesday morning. At its shallowest point, the reef is only 12 metres (37 feet) below the surface.

The ship leaked an estimated 13,400 tonnes of crude oil, making it the worst ever oil spill accident in Japan. One of the tanker's two ruptured oil storage tanks had stopped leaking but it was not clear if more crude oil was leaking from the other ruptured tank, the coastguard said.
The Diamond Grace was carrying 257,000 tonnes of crude oil from the United Arab Emirates to a refinery in Kawasaki, between Yokohama and Tokyo.
The single-hull tanker, built in 1994, was chartered by Mitsubishi Oil and operated by a subsidiary of Japan's largest shipping company, Nihon Yusen KK.
